$comment: Vectors of the contributor page's about block (1.2.0; ops decision D163; schemas/contributor-page-about.v1.json): what a renderer draws from our versioned words and the page document. The words are the texts file's at `version`, which `textsSha256` names by the SHA-256 of its bytes, so this file moves with every new version.

`sentences`: the proof sentence and the invite composed from a document's sections. `input.sections` is the slice of `contributor-page.v1` `sections` the rule reads (a certificates item's `status`, the repositories section's rows, the summary's `projects`, the adopter items); `input.certificatesIssued` is the renderer's own knowledge of the plane (false on production until ops decision D160 item 8 opens certificates there). `expect.proof` and `expect.invite` are the sentences, null when left out, the invite with its link words as plain text; `expect.link` is the block's one link: the invite's words and path, `inSentence` true, or Learn more and the site's root where the invite is withheld.

`blocks`: whole blocks per variant, the heading and the paragraphs as drawn (link words as plain text), and the link. For `own`, `input.text` is the document's `about.text` and the paragraphs are the person's words, then our one line, which Learn more follows. A block whose paragraphs name the predecessor writes them on one line after a `lint` member, which is not part of the expected block: this repository's copy-lint reads its allow marker line by line.

`certificatesIssued`: whether certificates are issued on each plane a document names (`contributor-page.v1` `source`), as a renderer must know it today, and so whether the invite is drawn there: on the development planes (`fixture`) yes; on production (`platform`) not until ops decision D160 item 8 opens certificates there, whose act moves this line and the renderer's together; and the public sample (`sample`), a made-up page every site build draws, production's included, follows production. A vector's `input.certificatesIssued` is one of these values.

check:contributor-page recomputes every vector with its own reading of the rule (not the renderer). The strings of `blocks` AB-1 to AB-5 and of every sentence are the ones the texts' claim check passed (design D163-ABOUT-TEXTS-2026-10-16, version 2).

expect.heading: The purpose behind this work
paragraphs: Open source already helps people. Under Purpose Source, the work on this page can do even more good, for people its makers may never meet.

Anyone may use, change and share it under its licence. It stays free for personal use, smaller organisations, non-profits, state schools, universities and public bodies in their own work. Large companies that use it pay a published fee, which maintainers can waive for any organisation they choose. The fees fund listed charities, chosen within seven areas of care: health, education, poverty relief, humanitarian aid, the environment, animal welfare and research. Every cost and every transfer is published.

The people who build the software keep their copyright, and maintainers keep control. Each release also becomes available under Apache-2.0 four years after its publication. No one is paid from these fees for a contribution. Contributors are credited instead, and have a say in the causes their work supports.

Further down, you will find my certificates and the projects that credited me: proof of my part in this work. If you contribute to Purpose Source projects, you can earn certificates for your own work too.
